The flowering shrub '''''Acalypha californica''''' is known as the '''California copperleaf''', and sometimes by the older name '''Pringle three-seeded mercury'''. It is the only ''Acalypha'' species native to California, where it is most abundant in the hills of [[San Diego County, California|San Diego County]]. It is a member of the [[Chaparral|chaparral plant community]].

The plant bears hairy, juicy, toothed leaves which despite the plant's common name are light green, never [[Copper (color)|copper]] in color. Each flower is made up of a [[Stamen|staminate]] part, which appears as a long spike of tiny red and pink [[bract]]s, and a [[Carpel|pistillate]] part at the base of the spike, which is a cup made up of green bracts bearing the ovary.

==Taxonomy==
''Acalypha californica'' was scientifically described and named in 1844 by [[George Bentham]].<ref name="POWO" /> The specimens he described were collected from [[Magdalena Bay]] in November 1837 during a voyage of [[HMS Sulphur (1826)|HMS Sulphur]] under the command of [[Edward Belcher]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bentham |first1=George |author-link1=George Bentham |last2=Belcher |first2=Edward |author-link2=Edward Belcher |date=1844 |editor-last1=Hinds |editor-first1=Richard Brinsley |editor-link1=Richard Brinsley Hinds |title=The Botany of the Voyage of H. M. S. Sulphur, Under the Command of Captain Sir Edward Belcher, During the Years 1836-42. Published under the authority of the Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/780211 |language=en-UK |location=London |publisher=Smith, Elder and Co. |pages=2, 4, 51–52 |oclc=741859007 |access-date=10 May 2026}}</ref> It is classified in the genus ''[[Acalypha]]'' within the [[Euphorbiaceae]] family. The species has no [[subspecies]] and has three [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]].<ref name="POWO">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=1150-2 |title=''Acalypha californica'' Benth. |access-date=10 May 2026}}</ref>

==Range and habitat==
California copperleaf is native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico.<ref name="POWO" /> In California it grows in just two southern counties, [[Orange County, California|Orange]] and [[San Diego County, California|San Diego]] counties, while in Arizona it is found in just [[Pima County, Arizona|Pima County]].<ref name="NRCS">{{cite usda plants|symbol=ACCA3 |title=Acalypha californica |date=10 May 2026}}</ref> It is native to all four states of northwestern Mexico, [[Baja California]], [[Baja California Sur]], [[Sonora]], and [[Sinaloa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hassler |first1=Michael |date=30 March 2026 |title=''Acalypha californica'' in the Synonymic Checklist and Distribution of the World Flora. Version 26.03 |url=http://www.worldplants.de?name=Acalypha-californica |website=World Plants |language=en |access-date=10 May 2026}}</ref>
